tier_reason: The headline compares two unrelated runs (an in-memory PostgreSQL run against a separate IO-bound MySQL run from Dimitri Kravtchuk's slides, known from a snippet only) and the pgtpc scripts do not reproduce as published, so no like-for-like measurement exists; directional only.

corrections.claimed_speedup: pgtpc Compare table point-select 1,814,404 vs 1,050,000 QPS (1.73x, derived) is not like for like: PostgreSQL fully in memory (95 GB prewarmed into 128 GB shared_buffers) vs an IO-bound MySQL Optane run from different slides; scripts do not reproduce as published.
corrections.caveats: Both sides durability-off; MySQL wins oltp_read_write; MySQL column headed TPS but holds QPS; loose fit for embedded-kv.

tier_reason: Tier stays C. Caveat correction: the web-table and full-text rows run Reindexer with the object cache forced on (ForceObjCache, AllowUnsafe(true)) while SQLite and MySQL unmarshal every row, so those rows are not a fair engine comparison; only the single-core by-ID, 1-condition and 2-condition rows unmarshal on both sides.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Single-core by-ID 4,224 ns/op vs SQLite 23,735 (5.6x) and Redis 47,492 (11.2x), 1-condition 3.5x, 2-condition 2.7x (derived from page data) stand; the web-table rows and the 32x full-text row serve cached object pointers against unmarshalling baselines and are not like for like.
corrections.caveats: SQLite ran on disk; Reindexer persists asynchronously (update gap is durability); harness imports an internal git.restream.ru path and cannot be rebuilt; sqlUpdate counts failed requests.

tier_reason: Raised D to C: an independent 2015 run (Howard Chu gist) measures Sophia 1.1 fillrandom at 1.5x LevelDB 1.17 (2.3x at 4000-byte values), but the run crashed before readrandom in both attempts, its sync row shows no per-write fsync, CPU and compiler are unstated and the build is a decade old, so it does not reach B; the original 2.6x read claim remains first-party and unmeasured.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Write: Sophia 1.1 fillrandom 74,143 vs LevelDB 1.17 48,930 ops/s (1.5x, derived from page data; HyperLevelDB 113,355), 4000-byte values 7,368 vs 3,187 (2.3x) in Howard Chu's 2015 gist. Read: first-party 438,084 vs 167,476 random reads/s (2.6x) never independently reproduced; the gist crashed before readrandom.
corrections.caveats: Sync row likely no per-write fsync; 26.2 GB on disk vs 14.3 GB for 16 GB of data; default makefile builds with -DSS_INJECTION_ENABLE -g and no NDEBUG; open crash issues #171, #54, #53; no tagged release.

tier_reason: Same defect as the PostgreSQL entry: the pgtpc read_write row compares a separate IO-bound MySQL run from Dimitri Kravtchuk's slides (snippet only) with a fully cached PostgreSQL run, and pgtpc's own pages disagree on the MySQL figure (900,000 vs about 780,000 QPS), so there is no like-for-like measurement; directional only.

corrections.claimed_speedup: pgtpc oltp_read_write MySQL.48C 900,000 vs PGSQL.48C 722,907 (1.25x, derived) comes from different runs (IO-bound MySQL Optane run vs cached PostgreSQL); with the PG log page's 780,000 figure the lead is about 1.08x.
corrections.caveats: No libmysqld in trunk, so not embeddable; loose fit for embedded-kv.

tier_reason: Tier stays C. Caveat correction: the largest wins (q20, q30) are parallelism (16 threads vs Neo4j capped at 4 vCPU in a VM) and index asymmetry (ART indexes for Ladybug, ID constraints only for Neo4j), per the user re-run in issue #1117.

corrections.caveats: q20 14.31 ms on 16 threads vs 103.68 ms on 1 thread (issue #1117 re-run); Neo4j capped at 4 vCPU, birthday stored as string, Bolt-to-VM floor about 1.22 ms; benchmarked 0.21.1 has the two-hop traversal regression (#1117).

tier_reason: Lowered C to D: the 2x over Dapper compares ODB on MySQL/Linux with Dapper's SQL Server numbers from a different machine and database, and the author's own SQL Server runs are slower than Dapper, so no like-for-like measurement supports a win; directional only.

corrections.claimed_speedup: ODB with MySQL 5.1.49 on Linux 24 ms per 500 iterations vs Dapper 47 ms on SQL Server (different machine and database); ODB 1.8.0 on SQL Server 222 ms (Win7) and 152 ms (Win2008R2) per 500, later about 65 ms derived, all slower than Dapper's 49 ms.
corrections.caveats: ORM, off-category in embedded-kv; SQLite pool shared-cache by default; GCC-plugin compiler picks gcc from PATH; NCUEL licence for Oracle and MSSQL.
